old: Quantum information and operator theory in finite dimensions provide the standard background \cite{NielsenChuang2010,Watrous2018,Bhatia1997}. Finite group projectors come from character theory \cite{Serre1977,FultonHarris1991}. Moving spectral subspaces and geometric phase originate in the work of Kato, Berry, Wilczek, and Zee \cite{Kato1950,Kato1995,Berry1984,WilczekZee1984}. Completely positive maps and quantum dynamical semigroups are treated in \cite{Stinespring1955,Choi1975,Kraus1983,Lindblad1976}. Exact error correction is governed by the Knill Laflamme condition \cite{KnillLaflamme1997,SchumacherNielsen1996,BenyKempfKribs2007}. Projection methods and hidden state memory are linked by the Feshbach, Nakajima, and Zwanzig constructions \cite{Feshbach1958,Nakajima1958,Zwanzig1960,BravyiDiVincenzoLoss2011}.

old: Error correction is expressed through compression to a code. Let \(P\) be the code projector. The class of \(PAP\) modulo scalar multiples of \(P\) measures the obstruction to making \(A\) undetectable within the code. The Knill Laflamme criterion says that this obstruction vanishes for every product \(E_a^*E_b\) from the error family. Diagonalizing the resulting positive coefficient matrix produces orthogonal syndrome packets and an explicit recovery on the error span.
